questions.problem:
The lengths of babies at birth in a given population are normally distributed with a mean of $\mu \,\text{cm}$ and a standard deviation of $6\,\text{cm}.$ Additionally, the length of $60%$ of the newborns falls between $0.9\mu \,\text{cm}$ and $1.1\mu \,\text{cm}.$ Find the mean $\mu $ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the length of a randomly selected newborn. Then we have $X∼N(\mu ,{6}^{2}),$ and we want to find the mean $\mu .$ 

We know that $P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu )=0.6.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.9\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ 2P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.6 \\ P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.3 \\ P(X<\mu )+P(\mu <X<1.1\mu ) & =0.5+0.3 \\ P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.1\mu ) & =0.8 \\ P(Z<\frac{0.1\mu }{6}) & =0.8 \\ Φ(\frac{0.1\mu }{6}) & =0.8 \\ \frac{0.1\mu }{6} & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.8)≈0.8416.
$$

Finally then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{0.1\mu }{6} & =0.8416 \\ 0.1\mu  & =5.0496 \\ \mu  & =\frac{5.0496}{0.1} \\  & ≈50.50\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A player's height in a particular professional basketball league is normally distributed with a mean of $77$ inches and a standard deviation of $3.57$ inches. What is the probability that the height of a randomly selected player is more than $76$ inches but less than $78$ inches? *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.06\,$ $\,0.07\,$ $\,0.08\,$
$\,0.1\,$ $\,0.5636\,$ $\,0.5675\,$ $\,0.5714\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.6026\,$ $\,0.6064\,$ $\,0.6103\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6406\,$ $\,0.6443\,$ $\,0.6480\,$
$z$ $\,0.06\,$ $\,0.07\,$ $\,0.08\,$
$\,-0.3\,$ $\,0.3594\,$ $\,0.3557\,$ $\,0.3520\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.3974\,$ $\,0.3936\,$ $\,0.3897\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4364\,$ $\,0.4325\,$ $\,0.4286\,$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the height (in inches) of a randomly selected player. Then we have $X∼N(77,{3.57}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(76<X<78).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(76<X<78) & =P(\frac{76-77}{3.57}<Z<\frac{78-77}{3.57}) \\  & =P(-0.28<Z<0.28)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.28<Z<0.28) & =P(Z<0.28)-P(Z\le -0.28) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.28)-P(Z\le -0.28) \\  & =Φ(0.28)-Φ(-0.28)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.28) & =0.6103 \\ Φ(-0.28) & =0.3897.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.28<Z<0.28) & =Φ(0.28)-Φ(-0.28) \\  & =0.6103-0.3897 \\  & =0.2206 \\  & ≈0.22\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the height of a randomly selected player is more than $76$ inches but less than $78$ inches is approximately $0.22.$

questions.problem:
The annual income of an employee in a large company is normally distributed with a mean of $$50\,000$ and a standard deviation of $$15\,000.$ What is the probability that a randomly selected employee's income is more than $$46\,700$ but less than $$56\,150?$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.4960\,$ $\,0.4920\,$
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.5793\,$ $\,0.5832\,$ $\,0.5871\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6179\,$ $\,0.6217\,$ $\,0.6255\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6554\,$ $\,0.6591\,$ $\,0.6628\,$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the annual income (in dollars) of a randomly selected employee. Then we have $X∼N(50\,000,15\,{000}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(46\,700<X<56\,150).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(46\,700<X<56\,150) & =P(\frac{46\,700-50\,000}{15\,000}<Z<\frac{56\,150-50\,000}{15\,000}) \\  & =P(-0.22<Z<0.41)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.22<Z<0.41) & =P(Z<0.41)-P(Z\le -0.22) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.41)-P(Z\le -0.22) \\  & =Φ(0.41)-Φ(-0.22)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.41) & =0.6591 \\ Φ(-0.22) & =0.4129.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.22<Z<0.41) & =Φ(0.41)-Φ(-0.22) \\  & =0.6591-0.4129 \\  & =0.2462 \\  & ≈0.25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected employee's income is more than $$46\,700$ but less than $$56\,150$ is approximately $0.25.$

questions.problem:
The average volume of soda in cans is $12$ ounces. Additionally, in $3%$ of cans, the soda volume is less than $11.7$ ounces. Assuming the volume of soda is normally distributed, find the percentage of cans containing less than $12.2$ ounces of soda, rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $p$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.10\,$ | $\,0.15\,$ | $\,0.20\,$ | $\,0.25\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ | $\,-1.8808\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8531\,$ | $\,0.8554\,$ | $\,0.8577\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8749\,$ | $\,0.8770\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8944\,$ | $\,0.8962\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the volume of soda in a randomly selected can. Then we have $X∼N(12,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X<12.2).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$

We know that $P(X<11.7)=0.03.$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<11.7) & =0.03 \\ P(Z\le \frac{11.7-12}{\sigma }) & =0.03 \\ Φ(\frac{-0.3}{\sigma }) & =0.03 \\ \frac{-0.3}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.03)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.03)≈-1.8808.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{-0.3}{\sigma } & =-1.8808 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & =6.26933 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1}{6.26933} \\  & ≈0.1595.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we can solve for $P(X<12.2)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<12.2) & =P(X\le 12.2) \\  & =P(Z\le \frac{12.2-12}{0.1595}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le 1.25) \\  & =Φ(1.25) \\  & ≈89.4%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $89.4%$  of soda cans contain less than $12.2$ ounces of soda.

questions.problem:
In electronics manufacturing, the average resistance of a certain type of resistor is $100\,Ω.$ However, $5%$ of resistors have resistance no more than $96.5\,Ω.$ Assuming that resistor resistances are normally distributed, find the standard deviation, $\sigma ,$ of the resistance, **rounded to two decimal places.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $\,p\,$ | $0.25$ | $0.20$ | $0.15$ | $0.10$ | $0.05$ | $0.01$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,{Φ}^{-1}(p)\,$ | $\,-0.6745\,$ | $\,-0.8416\,$ | $\,-1.0364\,$ | $\,-1.2816\,$ | $\,-1.6449\,$ | $\,-2.3263\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
$Ω$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the resistance (in ohms). Then we have $X∼N(100,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X\le 96.5)=0.05.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 96.5) & =0.05 \\ P(Z\le \frac{96.5-100}{\sigma }) & =0.05 \\ Φ(-\frac{3.5}{\sigma }) & =0.05 \\ -\frac{3.5}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.05).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.05)=-1.6449.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{3.5}{\sigma } & =-1.6449 \\ \frac{3.5}{\sigma } & =1.6449 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{3.5}{1.6449} \\  & ≈2.13\,Ω.\end{aligned}
$$
